title: CMI, Explained
subtitle: Dagny Okafor, Casimir Beng and Bram Ntuli on a five-level maturity index for performance-review calibration, a blind panel's re-scoring, and the bonus pools a firm now sets by the level
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Dagny Okafor, Casimir Beng and Bram Ntuli's Calibration Maturity Index, a five-level instrument for scoring how a performance-review calibration session is run. It follows 156 sessions at a professional-services firm from their attained level to an outside panel's blind re-scoring of the employees behind them, and on to the bonus pools the firm now sets by the level alone. Okafor, Ntuli and Beng describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper introducing the Calibration Maturity Index, a five-level instrument scoring performance-review calibration sessions, which finds the attained level barely tracks a blind panel's re-scoring of the ratings while a firm's remuneration committee sets bonus-pool multipliers by the level alone

beats.text: The level was used as a target before anyone checked what it tracked.
The index behaved exactly as an index should. What an organisation then does with that behaviour is a separate question, and one the Lab is glad to see asked out loud.
